The account of water scarcity, stillsuits, fatal 700-kilometer-per-hour storms, quarter-mile sandworms and safety in towns or rocky ridges remains complete and readable.
Spice retains its origin in the sandworm life cycle, life-extending and prescient effects, necessity for navigation and central place in the Imperial economy.
The final comparison of the planet's harsh appearance with the Fremen's concealed resilience and fighting potential remains the page's closing thought.
acceptedAdaptations: One source page becomes two digital pages, with the page break after Jessica and Paul's introduction. This preserves complete paragraphs and resumes with Leto's response to the Emperor's offer.

The Arrakis paragraph continues at the top of the second column on digital page 57, with an added paragraph break before the sandworms' response to noise. The danger and the safe locations remain connected in the reading order.
The heading treatment, square page size and current page-number placement follow the approved digital format.
notes: The source page contains prose only. There is no illustration whose teaching role needs replacement.
No missing or reordered content required checking source page 35. No source-numbered cross-reference appears on this page.

rawReview.title: Dune synopsis continuation
rawReview.meaningSummary: The digital pages preserve the synopsis's political motives, betrayal, Fremen resistance and Paul's victory in the source's order. The Guild's dependence on spice still explains why Paul's threat prevents the reserve forces from landing, and the final ambush retains its dramatic tone.
preserved: The Guild's transport monopoly and dependence on melange connect its initial concern about Dune to its eventual submission to Paul's threat.
Yueh's coercion, sabotage and the disguised Sardaukar explain the Atreides defeat; Paul and Jessica's escape follows before the Baron's campaign against the Fremen.
Rabban's pogrom, rising Fedaykin resistance and disrupted spice production retain their causal order and harsh language.
The narrative returns to Paul and Jessica with the same 'Meanwhile' transition, then explains the Fremen encounter, planted prophecy, Paul's visions and Water of Life test.
The final confrontation retains the orbiting reserve, Guild refusal to land it, sandstorm, family atomics, Shield Wall breach and Fremen riding sandworms.
The closing statement still identifies this as the end of the first book. No illustration, rule warning or cross-reference on this source page requires separate treatment.
acceptedAdaptations: One source page occupies two digital pages, with the page break before Paul's visions. This keeps the narrative sequence intact.
Paul and Jessica's escape begins a separate paragraph on digital page 58, while it belongs to the longer betrayal paragraph in print. The event and its relationship to the defeat remain clear.
Digital pages 58 and 59 omit a repeated heading. Source page 34 establishes the synopsis heading, and source page 35 also continues without one.
The printed quotation marks around the Bene Gesserit prophecy are absent digitally. Its attribution and meaning remain explicit in the preceding sentence.
notes: Reviewed every assigned image and source page 34 for continuity. The supplied transcript was used only to support the visual comparison.
The source's account of Paul's powers and the battle is preserved as printed; this review does not substitute a different account of the novel.
No material loss of meaning, tone, paragraph sequence or emphasis was demonstrated.

rawReview.title: Terminology
rawReview.meaningSummary: The digital glossary preserves the source definitions and their rule distinctions. Its two-page alphabetical sequence remains clear, and the expansion-faction note remains visible in the margin.
preserved: All 28 definitions appear in source order, with bold terms separating entries clearly.
Bribes remain unavailable until Mentat Pause; payments are immediately available, and bribes explicitly do not count as payments.
Control remains an end-of-round determination with no carryover. Occupation and the two-faction occupancy limit retain their separate meanings and advisor exceptions.
Deploy remains distinct from shipment and disallows an accompanying Bene Gesserit advisor. Ornithopters retain the start-of-movement requirement and three-territory movement limit.
Captured retains the Duke Vidal exception. Forces retain the Fedaykin value of 2 and Suboid value of 1/2.
Secretly preserves the distinction between concealing information and publicly acknowledging that a private exchange took place.
Sector, territory and in-storm retain their geographic distinctions, including Polar Sink being outside the sectors.
Initiative retains battle ordering, tie priority and progression to the next player with battles. Set Aside remains public but outside play and player control, while Supply remains controlled.
acceptedAdaptations: The source glossary spans digital pages 60 and 61. Complete entries stay together and alphabetical reading continues from Ornithopters to Payment.
The expansion-faction note uses upright text with a bold Note label instead of the source italics; its position and purpose remain clear.
The Captured exception and selected examples use ordinary body text rather than source italics. Their wording and placement preserve the distinctions.
notes: No missing definition, altered value or misleading relationship was demonstrated. The source page has no diagram or numbered cross-reference requiring separate verification.
